avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive antioxidant effects may increase bleeding risk and reduce edaravone efficacy through competitive free radical scavenging
avoid_supplements.action: Limit Vitamin E supplementation to <400 IU daily or consult prescriber before concurrent use

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Antiplatelet effects combined with edaravone's potential prothrombotic rebound may increase bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue ginkgo biloba or obtain cardiology clearance before edaravone therapy

caution_supplements.name: Curcumin/Turmeric
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additive antioxidant activity may theoretically potentiate effects but clinical significance unclear
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for enhanced therapeutic response; no dose adjustment typically required

caution_supplements.name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Both are antioxidants; potential synergistic neuroprotection but no known adverse interaction
caution_supplements.action: May be combined with monitoring; document concurrent use in patient record

caution_foods.name: High alcohol consumption
caution_foods.mechanism: Alcohol may impair free radical metabolism and increase oxidative stress, potentially reducing edaravone effectiveness
caution_foods.action: Counsel patient to limit alcohol intake to ≤1 drink daily during treatment course

monitoring_notes: Edaravone has minimal hepatic metabolism and no major CYP interactions, reducing supplement interaction risk. Monitor for signs of bleeding or thrombosis given the drug's vascular effects, particularly if combined with antiplatelet agents.
